text:
Detroit spent the second period taking the game apart, out-chancing Philadelphia 1.87 to 0.69 in expected goals, and still needed a defenseman's 14 percent look to get level. Anton Johansson's snap shot at 4:31, set up by Dylan Larkin and Justin Faulk, tied it after Matvei Michkov had given the Flyers a 1-0 lead late in the first on a snap shot that carried a 67 percent chance of going in.

The Red Wings won 2-1 and deserved it, taking 69 percent of simulated replays to Philadelphia's 31. They led in shot attempts 66 to 52, in shots on goal 26 to 18, and in total expected goals 3.63 to 2.5. At even strength the gap was wider, 2.57 to 1.31. Philadelphia's best stretch came in the third, where it edged the expected goals 0.93 to 0.85, but Andrew Copp's snap shot from Michael Rasmussen and Nate Danielson at 15:22 settled it. Copp was named first star.

Joseph Woll kept the Flyers in it, saving 1.63 goals more than the 26 shots against him deserved. Daniil Tarasov was good too, 1.5 above expected on 18 shots. Neither power play converted, Detroit going 0 for 4 and Philadelphia 0 for 2. Detroit gave the puck away 19 times to Philadelphia's six and still controlled the play, and Viktor Arvidsson missed the net on a 32 percent chance in the second that would have made the margin look more like the game.
